notes: Lane MN. name: gimex::bmp::ReadFrame (format 5, BMP: the pixels, bottom-up or top-down)
notes: Lane MN. Gimex_BmpRead (every depth, RLE8/RLE4, masks, bottom-up and top-down, cut files; pixels, result and stream position). 15 mutants, all killed. ORIGINAL-BUG: an RLE row whose padding is read at a buffer cursor that sits at the end of the row buffer overflows it by up to 3 bytes; those cases run on ours only. Hooked at its RVA (src/hook/tables/GimexBmp.cpp); our table (src/gz/Gimex.size.cpp) holds ours in the cell.

name: gimex::bmp::WriteFrame (format 5, BMP: headers, palette and pixel rows)
notes: Lane MN. Gimex_BmpWrite (every depth and mask layout, palettes, 1/4/8-bit run-length coding, rows up to 256 wide, write failures at every size; bytes written and result). 13 mutants: 11 killed (3 after the test was widened to rows of 250..261 pixels and constant rows), 2 equivalent (`4 <= remaining`: at remaining 4 the loop adds nothing that survives `run = remaining`; `remaining - 2 < run`: the only way the loop ends there is run == 0xfe, which the next clamp gives the same value). ORIGINAL-BUG: the original clears three times the last encoded row's length plus 16 bytes of a plain-row-sized buffer; a run-length coded last row that is more than 4 bytes longer than the plain row overruns the block, those cases run on ours only. Hooked at its RVA (src/hook/tables/GimexBmp.cpp); our table (src/gz/Gimex.size.cpp) holds ours in the cell.
